execution_note: The numerical stress was executed locally against an executable transcription of the frozen production V3 algorithms/constants and the same canonical CLOSED-row contract. The persisted validator dynamically imports the exact repository V3, reporter, and atomic-journal modules so the result is independently reproducible in a checked-out repository runtime. No deployment/runtime performance claim is made.

stress.adaptive_block_rule: B1=8; thereafter B=16 iff prior CLOSED block_score < 0.05 else B=4

interpretation: Binding the generic reporting wrapper to the V3 family leaves the original alpha=.05 two-channel decision-IUT numerically unchanged in the tested paths.

The separate .025/.025 simultaneous numeric-reporting contract is measurably stricter: in this finite synthetic condition it delayed the dual-bound safe report by a median 35 closed blocks and widened the two upper bounds by about 0.0044 and 0.0049 on average at the first decision-safe prefix.
The stricter numeric-reporting cost is a reporting-contract cost, not evidence that the existing threshold-20 AND decision is invalid or should split alpha.
scope_guards: The 60 campaigns are synthetic finite-condition stress, not observed production reliability or a universal stopping-time result.

The numerical result validates the V3 statistical family and adapter semantics, but exact repository-module execution should be rerun from the persisted validator when a checkout/runtime is available.
tau=.05, mismatch=.01 and missing=.002 are stress parameters, not recommended operational settings.
No forbidden semantic inputs were read; no downstream/O/other-worker state was used.
